        No. 1 Miami led the first College Football Playoff Rankings of 2026 season as one of only three undefeated teams remaining in the sport. The Hurricanes edge out No. 2 Georgia and fellow undefeated No. 3 Utah to rank at the top. Those three teams join No. 4 Indiana from the Big Ten as the four first-round byes in the College Football Playoff. As usual, the SEC received a stunning bump of contenders compared to the AP Top 25. Alabama ranked four spots ahead of their AP ranking, coming in at No. 5 in the first CFP Rankings. Kentucky sits at No. 6 and Texas No. 7, also multiple spots ahead of their AP Poll ranking. However, the most interesting part of the bracket comes at the end. Notre Dame projects as the last time into the College Football Playoff field as the 11-seed. Powerhouse Ohio State is the first team out of the bracket at No. 12, nudged out for top Group of Six championship No. 25 Boise State. Here is a look at how the College Football playoff bracket looks after the first CFP Rankings release of the 2026 season. The schools in this scenario that would host a first-round game are No. 5 Alabama, No. 6 Kentucky, No. 7 Texas and No. 8 UCLA. The first round of the CFP would pit Texas vs. Ole Miss in a rematch and have Alabama host the Group of Six representative.  
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Notre Dame must beat MiamiLast season, Notre Dame was the first team out of the College Football Playoff after finishing 10-2 with losses against two CFP squads. This year, the Fighting Irish are in an even more precarious situation coming out of the first rankings, sitting as the last team in the field. 
Notre Dame already has a loss to BYU on its schedule, and now plays No. 1 Miami on Saturday. If the Fighting Irish don't beat the top team in the nation, they're nearly a lock to miss the postseason. Notre Dame's only other potential positive data points -- SMU and Wisconsin -- both lost last weekend. They're already in the danger zone. The SEC is getting lots of creditThe CFP committee typically gives the SEC a little bump compared to the AP rankings, but this year was a whole different level. Four SEC teams ranked in the top seven of the CFP Rankings, compared to one in the AP Top 25. Alabama was the biggest winner, ranking at No. 5 in the CFP Rankings despite two losses, three spots ahead of their AP poll ranking. No. 6 Kentucky and No. 7 Texas also moved up significantly. There are five SEC teams in the projected CFP field this year, and No. 13 Tennessee and No. 14 LSU ensure that the league will get plenty of teams in. 
What would a 24-team field look like?The College Football Playoff field will be 12 teams for at least one more season, but Yahoo Sports mocked up what a larger expansion could look like. The SEC would get nine teams into the field -- more than half the league.

title: College Football Playoff Rankings reaction: Notre Dame among underrated teams slighted, SEC's efforts succeed - CBS Sports
description: The selection committee gave the SEC plenty of love with its new metric, leaving Notre Dame with no room for erro
body:
The selection committee gave the SEC plenty of love with its new metric, leaving Notre Dame with no room for error and two-loss Alabama sitting way too high
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 3, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:19 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Welcome to the first of five weeks of College Football Playoff frustration. The selection committee released its first Top 25 of the season Tuesday, and with five more to go until Selection Sunday, there's plenty to digest.Those who forget the past are doomed to repeat it, so a quick lesson before we overreact to the first rankings of the 2026 season. Last season taught us a clear lesson: never take a team's ranking at face value until Selection Sunday.It's easy to forget the magic trick the CFP pulled last fall, when they proved head-to-head results matter only when convenient. For five weeks, Miami trailed Notre Dame in the CFP's Top 25, even though the Hurricanes owned a head-to-head win in Week 1. On Selection Sunday, the CFP committee finally flipped the two, and Miami earned the final at-large spot in the playoff, jumping two spots despite not playing in the ACC Championship Game.Why? The committee's feelings — fueled by internal debate — were supported by their myriad metrics. Those metrics, by the way, are not available for public consumption.
On Tuesday night, we discovered a new metric that will fuel disruption: the strength-of-conference rating. Will that stick? History says no, because the committee changes its mind week to week. So, buckle up. If you're upset your favorite team is ranked lower than it deserves, or if you're frustrated that a rival is slotted higher than it deserves, don't fret. Both can change at any time, based on one of many lines of logic supported by endless proprietary data the CFP sees, but you don't.Feel hopeless? Don't! Embrace debate! The warning signs have been visible for years.
"Obviously, college football has the most passionate fan bases across the country," CFP selection chairman Hunter Yurachek explained mere moments after the CFP pushed Miami ahead of Notre Dame last December. "Everyone can spin the metrics in favor of the team or teams that they support. So you're always going to have controversy. "Here's what we didn't like about the first iteration of the CFP's Top 25 released Tuesday night, before an impactful Week 10 slate of games:For better or worse, the SEC's lobbying workedThe SEC lobbied hard over the last two years to introduce new metrics for the committee to use. Well, it worked. The strength-of-conference metric has apparently been the buoy that lifted the conference to heights no other power conference has been afforded. 
All six two-loss SEC teams are ranked higher than they are in both the AP and coaches polls this week. Two two-loss teams (No. 5 Alabama and No. 7 Texas) rank higher than undefeated UCLA at No. 8.Heck, the SEC has the highest-ranked two- and three-loss teams with Alabama and No. 21 South Carolina. If a 24-team playoff were played tonight, nine of 16 teams (!) from the SEC would be in the field.The issue here is the CFP said this new data point would be an enhancement, not necessarily a new metric, but it played out Tuesday as the biggest differentiator between the SEC teams and everyone else. The declaration when it was introduced months ago and the rankings released Tuesday do not match.
If this strength-of-conference metric continues to carry weight, expect some peeved-off fans in the other conferences at the end of the season.The committee continues to slight Notre DameIf it wasn't clear already, the Fighting Irish can't afford a loss this week against No. 1 Miami. Notre Dame debuted at No. 11 in the initial rankings, and the reasoning was simple."They don't have that signature win," Yurachek said Tuesday. Still, that's a bit low, right? That's a full seven spots lower than the AP poll, by far the biggest difference in the initial CFP Rankings. The loss to BYU hurts, and the Cougars' subsequent loss at UCF doesn't help, but why the disconnect from voters in the AP and coaches polls?The Irish have only one game remaining against a top 25 team: Miami this week. That win will be enough to lift the Irish into the playoff, and I suspect they will be in the top five with a victory against the Hurricanes on Saturday, but the margin for error is absolute zero. SMU tumbling out of the AP rankings with a loss to Syracuse last week hurts the Irish, who face the Mustangs later this season.
I counter with Indiana at No. 4. The Hoosiers' resume is not strong, much like their in-state rivals, so why are we rewarding the reigning national champions while punishing the Irish?This sets up another disappointment for the Irish, one way or another. Even with a win against Miami, something tells me Notre Dame could slide in the rankings in the third, fourth and fifth rankings before Selection Sunday. The committee has done it before with teams that keep winning. Heck, it happened to the Irish last season. Strength of record matters.Alabama is overratedNo. 5 Alabama is hanging its hat on a — *checks notes* — road win at Kentucky. The two-loss Tide debuted four spots higher than they were ranked in the AP and coaches polls.
The Tide are 2-2 against teams in the CFP's Top 25. The committee chairman said they were impressed by Alabama's win at Mississippi State. Huh? Remember, MSU was not at full strength; quarterback Kamario Taylor was injured, and the Bulldogs went winless in October. How is that a signature win? It meets none of the criteria the committee examines.Six — six! — teams below Alabama own better records against the CFP Top 25.We expected Kentucky to be ranked higher with one loss than Alabama with two, even with the head-to-head win. Then again, the committee doesn't weigh head-to-head results as much as we assume. Yurachek admitted that Tuesday while discussing Indiana and Ohio State's head-to-head matchup in which the Buckeyes won.Ohio State should be angryIf the playoff started today, Ohio State would not be a participant. The same Buckeyes team that defeated reigning national champion Indiana, now No. 4 in the CFP's rankings, appeared at No. 12 and the first team out of the field. 
The Buckeyes own the nation's ninth-best strength of record and 18th-best schedule, according to the same numbers ESPN flashes across the screen as they reveal the CFP rankings. Amazingly, only two Big Ten teams are in the CFP today compared to the SEC's five. Talk all you want about Ohio State playing without quarterback Julian Sayin, but the Buckeyes defeated Indiana on the road in the fourth quarter without their starter."We never got to a point where we were comparing Indiana and Ohio State in their head-to-head," Yurachek said Tuesday night.
Oh, boy. That won't sit well in Columbus, Ohio.We need to talk about UCLAUCLA is undefeated and ranks eighth. Utah is undefeated and ranks third. They're five spots apart. And there's one big difference – but it actually favors the Bruins.UCLA's strength of schedule ranks 77th. Utah is 83rd. So, why are the Bruins five spots lower? I understand Utah being higher because of its recent win against Houston, but the metrics seem to favor the Bruins elsewhere, and they've done it several weeks playing their backup quarterback.Where's New Mexico?New Mexico is the only team ranked in the AP poll (22nd) to not appear in the CFP's Top 25. That's not shocking, but why are three teams with three losses ranked above a one-loss Mountain West team whose only loss was by a touchdown on the road to the SEC's Oklahoma? After all, the committee showed Tuesday night that the SEC is the toughest conference in the country, so why isn't New Mexico rewarded with a top-25 ranking?

body:
Sharing the touchline brought a historic league title and a Champions League draw with Bayern Munich to Norway, proving two voices can be better than one
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:16 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Are two coaches better than one? This is a question that teams around the world, like Viking FK, are trying to answer as they bring dual head coaches to the big stage in Champions League play. The Norwegian side aren't alone in their exploits, as Lyngby in Denmark and Lincoln City in the English Championship are a few of the clubs to join in employing dual head coaches, but they're among the most notable, as Morten Jensen and Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim were able to lead the club to a 3-3 draw with Bayern Munich in Champions League play. There may just be a method to the madness.Viking were trailblazers on the pitch, appointing the duo in 2020, and they helped lead the club to their first Norwegian league title in 34 years, which sent them into the Champions League for this campaign. Jensen and Aarsheim had chances to interview for the role, but being good friends off the pitch, they suggested taking it on together, a situation that the club has no regrets about as they add to the improving stature of Norwegian soccer."When the former coach left us, we knew we needed another coach, and we started the interview process. We brought the two assistant coaches in for different interviews, and then when the interview came, they just showed up together," club CEO Eirik Bjorno said, reminiscing on how this came to be to CBS Sports Golazo in September. "It was their idea. We said we needed to pick one of you, and they said that they were going to do it together. At the end, we said, 'Let's do it.' It has been fairly successful so far; there is no difference between them. They are both head coaches. It's fascinating when we have discussions: I discuss one thing with one of them, and then another thing with the other one, and then we sit down all together to find a solution. I just created more work for myself; I don't recommend it, to be honest."But while they took a route of forcing the club's hand due to their own relationship and wanting to work together, that's not the only way for this to come to be. At Lyngby, the club wanted to install a dual setup when their manager, Morten Karlsen, was fired in December of 2025. Andreas Bjelland was already at the club as an assistant but had never held a head coaching role. When Mikkel Jespersen was recently let go from Mainz, the club reached out. As Jespersen described it, "We talked about life, football, everything just to see if there was a connection, and luckily there was, and we took it from there step by step, and we jumped into the cooperation."
Bjelland echoes how important it was for those meetings to go well before they jumped into managing Lyngby."Because you have to work really closely, it also has to be a person that you work quite well with and can understand and talk to in all kinds of different matters in life," Bjelland said. "So the meetings leading up to the co-coaching were the thing that gave the right feeling."The duo may not be breaking down the door for the Champions League yet, but their leadership led the club to promotion back to the Danish Superliga, Denmark's top flight, while they're also helping shape the future of American soccer, as USMNT international Neil Pierre was part of the promotion-winning setup and Diego Kochen is currently the starting keeper for the club while on loan from Barcelona. The club hasn't won the Superliga since the 1991-92 season, so their path mirrors an early stage of Viking's, where the immediate goal is steady improvement in order to establish themselves back in the top flight, and the teamwork that Jespersen and Bjelland bring to the club makes them well positioned to do so.
"We're quite different. I think that's one of the things as well that really makes a good team, is that as persons we're quite different and how we act in front of the players, our personalities and all that stuff," Bjelland says. "A little bit like a relationship that you have to be different than your partner, else it wouldn't work. And that's for me a little bit the same, even though we don't hug and kiss. We still have to know a lot about each other, but being different is also a big thing about it that gives us all the tools that we have, so that we can cover more."Balancing the RolesDifferences in management are what bring a major challenge to balancing these roles. Bjorno spoke about needing to meet with both coaches about the same topics at Viking, and they've also opened up about how they need to work through disagreements when it comes to coaching decisions. You can't go out to the squad with one coach wanting to go in one direction while the other wants to go in the opposite, and that level of conflict resolution is something that these clubs go through behind closed doors ahead of time."Then we'll discuss, loudly sometimes, with the rest of our staff in the coaching room, and we will both have to defend our choices and reasoning to them," Jensen said in an interview with the Guardian. "We'll all discuss it until we have an agreement. But 99% of the time, we are pretty agreed in terms of who to use in a particular game, so it's very seldom we waste time over that."
Aarsheim added, "I can read Morten in one second. If he really wants something from his stomach, then I sense it: 'OK, let's go with that.' It's never been a problem."It's similar at Lyngby, where the coaches have created a structure between themselves."We need to be really aligned in everything we do, and then the roles have to be really clear," Bjelland said. "So every day we know exactly who's doing what. So Mikkel has a lot of the things against the ball on minus three, and then I would have on the ball minus two. So everything we do is really structured. Of course, we discuss everything, and it takes some extra talks, and it takes some extra work to do, so we have to be pretty aligned in everything that we say and do."
The trust to know that a coach is saying what you'd expect when meeting with players is something that's built through working together, and when done well, it can make the job easier for those involved because you have someone to brainstorm with and work on tactical decisions with. In life, it's natural to have someone who can be a sounding board, and while assistant coaches can do that too, it's a different power dynamic than when someone is in the same position as you as a head coach."Yeah, it is. Especially when it's the first time both of us are head coaches," Jespersen said on the comfort of having a dual manager in charge with him. "It's nice to have each other to talk everything through. Also, when you're in doubt, it's nice to have someone who maybe has the same doubts as you to make the right decision."It takes a particular style of group to make it work, but these clubs are using it with success, and it could be something that others try to emulate. Watching Viking perform and manage this at the highest level, others have already followed, with Lyngby and Lincoln City moving in the dual head coach direction in the past year. If that continues to catch on,  we may be seeing the buds of a new coaching revolution in the global game.

        Another Champions League matchday is partially in the books. There are some teams that are already halfway through the league phase, which will last until January. It's important to remember that only the top eight teams will qualify directly for the knockout rounds, while those finishing between ninth and 24th place will have to compete in a two-legged playoff in February to secure their place in the next stage. Let's now take a look at some of the big European teams and see how much they should be worried ahead of the remaining four league phase games. AS Roma The Giallorossi lost again in the final minutes of a Champions League match. Gian Piero Gasperini's side repeated the same mistakes they made last month at the Stadio Olimpico against Real Madrid, when they conceded three goals late in the second half after being up 3-1. Something similar happened against Manchester United at Old Trafford, as AS Roma lost 3-2 after scoring the first two goals of the game. Next up is a trip to PSG at the Parc des Princes, and it's difficult to imagine them bringing any points back to Rome. With four points collected after four games, they should start to worry a bit now. Panic level: 7/10 😤Atletico MadridThey are in a better spot than AS Roma. Diego Simeone's side have been quite disappointing so far, losing to Liverpool away and to Bayern Munich at home, though they did beat Manchester United in Madrid earlier. Clearly, they had a very challenging first half of the league phase, but they now have a much more doable path: Viking, PSV and Bodo/Glimt, before facing Fenerbahce in their last away game of the league phase. They should aim to finish in the top 16 at the very least.Panic level: 6/10 🤕InterAfter defeats against Real Madrid and Club Brugge in the opening two games of the league phase, the Nerazzurri won two in a row against Shakhtar and, most notably, 3-0 away at Feyenoord. That win came a few days after Inter lost the Derby della Madonnina 3-1 to AC Milan, a defeat that raised many doubts about Cristian Chivu's management following some disappointing performances early in the season. However, the win against Feyenoord put things in a much better place for Inter, who will now host Stuttgart at San Siro before facing Borussia Dortmund away, Liverpool in Milan and Slavia Prague in the final match of the league phase.Panic level: 5/10 🤩Man UnitedOn the other hand, things finally look a bit better for Manchester United after beating AS Roma at Old Trafford. However, the big question now is: has Michael Carrick left it too late? Things will be clearer in the coming days, especially ahead of the November international break. The Red Devils have some challenging matches left in the league phase, with visits to Sporting CP and Villarreal plus home games against RB Leipzig and, most notably, Bayern Munich. It's certainly not over for them yet, but at least they can now look ahead with a little more optimism.
Panic level: 6/10 😡

        We've been on the wrong side of a couple of bad beats throughout the first half of the regular season, and Week 8 was no exception. One of my five locks last week was the Patriots covering a 7.5-point spread over the Dolphins in Miami. For a large chunk of the second half, we were well on our way to cashing. Then, in the blink of an eye, we were suddenly sweating it out. After a 14-point third-quarter lead ballooned New England's lead to 11 and just four minutes remained in regulation, the Dolphins put together an eight-play, 84-yard touchdown drive to cut it within five. The gut punch was Malik Willis uncorking a 35-yard touchdown to Kevin Coleman Jr. to put them within the number. 
Even when all was thought to be lost, there was another opportunity for New England to extend the lead late after a botched onside kick by Miami. The Patriots reached the Dolphins' 38-yard line and faced a third-and-5. If they failed to convert, a meaningless field-goal attempt would've brought the lead to eight. Alas, Rhamondre Stevenson rushed for the necessary yardage to move the chains, Drake Maye knelt three times, and we came out losers. Pain. While that bat beat put in through a torture chamber, it was a good slate for us overall. I was 3-2 ATS with my locks of the week, 8-6 ATS overall, and 10-4 on the moneyline. I'll look to keep that momentum rolling and try to avoid any more bad beats as our attention now pivots to Week 9. As always, we begin with my five locks of the week. 
Note: Tennessee and Pittsburgh are on the bye in Week 9.All lines via DraftKings; All times ET2026 recordLocks of the Week ATS: 20-19-1ATS: 53-65-3ML: 75-45-1Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago BearsSunday, 8:20 p.m. (NBC, Stream: Fubo, try for free)The Bears look like bona fide Super Bowl contenders right now after rolling into Seattle and taking it to the defending champion Seahawks, with new defensive stud Jeffery Simmons showing out in his debut. They head back home for another primetime matchup against a Bucs team that didn't complete a pass in a 16-0 win over the Falcons. Over the past two games, Tampa Bay's passing attack has completed 7 of 14 attempts for 64 yards and one touchdown. That might be good enough to lock in two wins against NFC South rivals, but they'll need to chuck it to keep pace with Caleb Williams and keep this newly dominant defense honest. I don't believe they will be able to, which sets up Chicago to win its fourth straight game. The Bears are also 3-1 ATS at home this season.Projected score: Bears 28, Buccaneers 20The pick: Bears -6.5Green Bay Packers at New England PatriotsSunday, 4:25 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo, try for free)Weather was a factor, but I did find it noteworthy that the Patriots struggled to fend off the Dolphins in last week's win in Miami. Sure, a divisional game will always be pesky, but it is sticking in the back of my head as I look towards this matchup with Green Bay. 
I think Drake Maye, who leads the NFL in total yards and total touchdowns from Week 4 to Week 8, will have some trouble against this evolving Packers defense. Over the past five games, Green Bay is allowing just 14.6 points per game, which ranks third in the NFL. Meanwhile, Jordan Love is first in the NFL in passing yards entering Week 8 and first in completions of 20-plus air yards. He's also fourth in passing touchdowns, so New England's defense will have its hands full and is firmly on upset alert. Projected score: Packers 23, Patriots 21The pick: Packers +3Los Angeles Rams at Washington CommandersSunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo, try for free)Jayden Daniels was pretty erratic with his throws on Sunday night, despite pulling out the 27-10 win over Philadelphia. For the game, he had an off-target rate of 17.2%, which was the third-highest in a single game in his career. That's alarming, particularly as Washington hosts a Rams team that is starting to gain some momentum. This season, L.A. is allowing 301.1 total yards per game, which ranks fifth in the league. If Daniels continues to misfire, this Rams defense has shown it can shut down an opponent. Meanwhile, the Commanders are 0-5 following a win since the start of last season and own a -9.0 points-per-game differential over that stretch. 
This could be a game where Matthew Stafford and Puka Nacua feast, as Washington is currently giving up a 100.6 passer rating against this season, which ranks 25th in the league. I expect another prolific game from that duo as L.A. wins and covers. Projected score: Rams 27, Commanders 21The pick: Rams -5.5Dallas Cowboys at Indianapolis ColtsSunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo, try for free)At any moment, another star could be shipped out of Indy, which makes this line something we'll want to jump on with it below a touchdown. Yes, the Cowboys defense is horrid and just lost to Gardner Minshew and the Cardinals, but Indianapolis is lost right now. They were just blown out 42-7 by the Jaguars and are 2-13 over their past 15 games. This season, they are allowing 27.8 points per game, which is the third-highest in the NFL entering Week 9. That sets up this Cowboys offense to flirt with 30 points on the day. If they get there, it's hard to imagine Daniel Jones keeping pace, even when accounting for Dallas' defense. Jones has an NFL-worst 68.7 passer rating this season and appears to be barely clinging to his starting job. Since Week 9 of last year, Jones is 3-10 as the starter with 13 total touchdowns and 20 turnovers. Meanwhile, I think Indy will continue to limit Jonathan Taylor, with trade rumors still swirling around him. Last week, he played a season-low 62.3% of the offensive snaps, which was less than the 67.2% offensive snaps he logged the week prior in Week 7. If Taylor is less of a factor, that only lowers the ceiling of the Indy offense and clears a path for Dallas to cover. 
Projected score: Cowboys 30, Colts 17The pick: Cowboys -6Buffalo Bills at Minnesota VikingsMonday, 8:15 p.m. (ESPN, Stream: Fubo, try for free)The Vikings suffered their first loss of the season in Week 8, falling to the Lions in a game that further emphasized the clunky start Kyler Murray has had running the offense. It's largely been masked by the stellar play of the defense, but Minnesota's offense is averaging just 279.4 total yards per game, which is the fourth-lowest in the league. Their 20 points per game average ranks sixth-lowest. That's unsustainable, especially against another high-octane offense like the Bills. Buffalo is averaging a league-best 33.3 points per game. While the Vikings defense will make it hard for them to maintain that average, they may not need to reach 30 to pull out the win on the road. Last week, Detroit scored 19 points in the winning effort, while going 1-for-3 in the red zone. Buffalo scores touchdowns on 70% of its red zone trips this season (fifth-highest). title: CFP rankings winners and losers: Alabama's path widens, Notre Dame's takes a hit - CBS Sports
description: The College Football Playoff committee's first rankings sparked confusion, elevating some resumes while penalizin
body:
The College Football Playoff committee's first rankings sparked confusion, elevating some resumes while penalizing others with seemingly inconsistent logic
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:26 am ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Even after years of watching College Football Playoff Selection Committee chairmen attempt to explain the unexplainable, what transpired Tuesday night was stunning.In what's been a particularly chaotic season, you knew the first CFP Rankings had the chance to be extra wonky. There were new selection committee members, new metrics to consider, such as a new strength-of-conference data point, and lots of results that muddled understanding. And yet the committee still somehow delivered one of the most questionable first rankings we've ever seen. That feels like hyperbole, but the lack of consistency down the rankings defies belief. In some cases, the committee valued head-to-head results (Alabama vs. Kentucky); in others, it didn't (Alabama vs. Tennessee). In some situations, a weak schedule was punished (Notre Dame, UCLA), and in others it wasn't (Indiana). It's a great development for content creators everywhere who can capitalize on the outrage over the rankings, but tough for those who wanted a more cohesive and clear approach from the committee. 
The good news is a lot can change between Nov. 3 and Dec. 6 when we get the final CFP Rankings. This weekend alone could have a dramatic impact on the next rankings with a stacked slate that includes No. 1 Miami at No. 11 Notre Dame, No. 2 Georgia at No. 10 Ole Miss, No. 5 Alabama at No. 14 LSU, No. 9 BYU at No. 3 Utah and No. 6 Kentucky at No. 13 Tennessee. Before we consider what future rankings might look like, though, here are the big winners and losers from the first edition of the 2026 College Football Playoff Rankings. 
        
            
                College Football Playoff bracket: What 12-team field would look like after first 2026 CFP rankings
                
                    Shehan Jeyarajah                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner -- AlabamaAlabama given more credit than expected, wider playoff pathThe stunner of the night came when 6-2 Alabama landed at the No. 5 spot. A sampling of teams Alabama is ranked ahead of:No. 7 Texas (6-2) No. 8 UCLA (8-0)No. 9 BYU (7-1)No. 10 Ole Miss (6-2)No. 13 Tennessee (6-2)You could make an argument that any and all of those teams should be ranked ahead of Alabama. Let's focus on the SEC teams, given there are more common opponents. Texas has three top-25 wins, which include a road win over the same Tennessee team that manhandled Alabama, 26-10. It's only a two-spot difference, but Texas clearly has a better resume right now than Alabama.
Tennessee has a head-to-head win over Alabama and yet is eight spots below the Tide in the rankings. The selection committee gets around the issue by claiming that Alabama and Tennessee are in different pods and thus not directly comparable, so head-to-head would not come into play. If Tennessee wins this weekend, however, it should make that argument moot. Alabama has two top-25 wins (Kentucky, South Carolina) but the committee is intent on giving it credit for a third. CFP chair Hunter Yurachek referenced Alabama beating Mississippi State on the road when the Bulldogs were 4-0 and ranked No. 16. "They were 4-0," Yurachek said on a teleconference about Mississippi State. "They had gone on the road and really dismantled a Minnesota team and looked very good doing so. I think maybe 'GameDay' had gone to that. It was a big game to play Alabama at home, and Alabama went in there and really took care of business and dominated that game. The committee, I think, will always view that as a quality game regardless of what the computer may say about the strength of that game."
It's a compliment to Mississippi State, which is now 4-4, that the committee will always treat it as a quality win for Alabama regardless of whether it finishes above .500. It is worth noting, however, that star quarterback Kamario Taylor was already injured by that point and wasn't playing at full strength in a game Alabama won 56-23. Taylor has since been ruled out for the season after undergoing foot surgery. Coming into the week, it felt like Alabama vs. LSU was a playoff eliminator type game. But Alabama now has more cushion than expected and could still make the field at 9-3 even if it loses to the Tigers this weekend. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser -- Notre DameFighting Irish's playoff outlook takes major hitWe've been beating the drum since Saturday that Notre Dame was potentially in trouble, but Tuesday night's rankings were even more dire than expected. Despite being ranked No. 4 in the AP poll, Notre Dame landed at No. 11 in the CFP Rankings. That leaves zero margin of error moving forward. 
If the Fighting Irish can't beat Miami, they will almost certainly not be in the field. There simply isn't a marquee win opportunity left on the schedule after Miami, and it is clear that the committee values strength of schedule more than efficiency statistics that rate ND highly. Notre Dame has zero top-25 wins, and without one over No. 1 Miami, it will finish without one. SMU losing to Syracuse last weekend was incredibly damaging. Notre Dame is your biggest loser in the first rankings. Winner -- SECThe committee values SEC schedules and résumésAlabama was the night's biggest winner, but the SEC has to be happy with what it saw. The conference put seven teams in the CFP top 15 and would have five teams in the playoff field if the season ended today. The SEC hasn't hidden its frustration in recent years with what the selection committee prioritized in picking the field. It was especially bad with the 2024 field, but there was frustration again a year ago when 9-3 Texas and 10-2 Vanderbilt both missed the cut. The SEC didn't think CFP selection committee members did a good enough job properly taking into account just how hard it was to play an SEC schedule week in and week out.
The message seemed to be heard loud and clear in the CFP's first 2026 rankings. There appeared to be a greater emphasis on strength of schedule, a metric that benefits the SEC's top teams. It was also interesting to hear Yurachek note, "I know the SEC is 10-2 in those games" about Power Four versus non-conference Power Four opponents while also claiming those weren't taken into account collectively for the conference. The new strength-of-conference metric is vague but would seem to take a statistic like that into account. The SEC is the clear best Power Four conference this season, and that was well reflected in these rankings. There will be a shake-up after all the top 25 games involving SEC teams this weekend, but the conference is well-positioned to have a sizable number of teams in the official field. It begs the question of whether the SEC knew it would be as respected as it seems to be so far this season, and whether it would have been as inclined to go along with a playoff expansion to 24 teams. Loser -- Big TenSeveral contenders were ranked lower than expectedThe conference that has won the last three national championships got the benefit of the doubt with Indiana, but that was it. There is now a very real possibility the Big Ten is only a two-bid league, which would have seemed inconceivable at the start of the season when Ohio State and Oregon were ranked No. 1 and 2, respectively. The No. 23 Ducks (5-3) are now, at best, a long shot to make the field. No. 12 Ohio State is the first team out and must beat Oregon this weekend to keep its playoff hopes alive. 
Ohio State sure seems to be getting heavily penalized for losing quarterback Julian Sayin. Yurachek referenced the defense giving up some explosive plays as part of the rationale for the Buckeyes' ranking. Frankly, it's a nonsensical data point, given that Ohio State gives up fewer explosive plays than five teams ranked ahead of it. No. 11 Ole Miss, for instance, ranks 104th nationally in explosive play rate allowed compared to Ohio State's No. 37. Ohio State has one of the best wins of the country (Indiana) and yet doesn't seem to be getting much credit for it. It was a bit surprising, too, to see undefeated UCLA land at No. 8. The Bruins' resume is lacking -- just one top-25 win -- but it's still a tough pill to swallow for the Big Ten to see two 2-loss SEC teams ranked ahead of its lone undefeated squad. It also sets the stage for UCLA to possibly drop out of the field in the Big Ten's ultimate doomsday scenario if the Bruins lose a game or two down the stretch. USC, coming off a win over Ohio State, feels about four or five spots too low at No. 20, too. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner -- IndianaHoosiers rewarded for their record despite a lack of marquee winsThe Hoosiers are getting a lot of benefit from their record against "quality" opponents with better-than-.500 records. On paper, Indiana hasn't beaten anyone of note. The Hoosiers don't have a single win over a team ranked in the CFP top 25. Even worse, Indiana hasn't passed the "eye test" at any point this season and has struggled against lesser opponents. But the Hoosiers do have five wins over teams that have winning records, a statistic the committee evidently greatly values. 
That was enough to get Indiana ranked No. 4 and in line for a first-round bye. That's eight spots better than an Ohio State team that the Hoosiers lost to earlier this season. The Hoosiers have a great strength of record (No. 5) and a solid strength of schedule (No. 32) but have rarely looked like an elite team this season. Indiana easily could have lost to three unranked opponents this season -- Northwestern, Nebraska and Minnesota. If Indiana wins out and wins the Big Ten Championship, this No. 4 slot would make a lot of sense. But as things stand in early November, this ranking is a reach. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser -- Texas TechOnly loss hurting Red Raiders' chancesThe 7-1 Red Raiders have to be disappointed to be starting out at No. 15. Texas Tech has wins over two top-25 teams, headlined by No. 17 Houston, and yet is behind a two-loss LSU team that has zero. "I think you'll have to really lean on the loss that (Texas Tech) had at Cincinnati two weeks ago for that reason," Yurachek said. 
It is fair to hold the Cincinnati loss against Texas Tech, but the Red Raiders deserve to be ranked a little better. Landing at No. 15 makes the path to getting into the field more challenging with zero opportunities to add a marquee win in the regular season. The remaining schedule is very manageable, making an 11-1 finish possible for Texas Tech and likely a requirement if it wants to make the field. With three teams ranked in the top 15, we could see two or more Big 12 teams get in. It'll be very interesting to see what happens in next week's rankings if BYU beats Utah this weekend. The CBS Sports forecasting model still prefers Texas Tech's playoff chances (62.7%) to BYU's (48.4%), but a Cougars win could keep both BYU and Utah ahead of the Red Raiders.

The Buckeyes, by the way, would be out of the playoff if the season ended today.Joe Fagnano will start for the Ravens in Week 9. The injury situation in Baltimore's quarterback room is rough with Lamar Jackson out as he undergoes thumb surgery and Tyler Huntley on the shelf with turf toe. Fagnano, an undrafted rookie, was the emergency third QB on Sunday and is now suddenly thrust into the starting lineup for the first time. For depth behind him, the Ravens added another undrafted signal-caller in Kedon Slovis off the Packers' practice squad. As this team attempts to stay afloat during Jackson's prolonged absence, it could be one to watch ahead of the trade deadline. Landing a premier backup like Tyson Bagent would come at a hefty price, though.The Mariners hired a skipper with no managerial experience. It's a bold strategy for a club that aims to get over the hump and win its first World Series. Cubs director of player development Jason Kanzler is the choice for the job and will replace Dan Wilson, who left the team after he oversaw the most disappointing 2026 season of any team in MLB. At 36, Kanzler is the second-youngest manager in baseball. Former Astros manager Joe Espada was reportedly the other finalist.UEFA Champions League Matchday 4 featured a stunning comeback. title: MLB offseason bold predictions: Tarik Skubal, William Contreras, Yankees, more - CBS Sports
description: With the offseason underway, Mike Axisa pulls out his crystal ball and predicts how the winter will go
body:
With the offseason underway, Mike Axisa pulls out his crystal ball and predicts how the winter will go
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:45 am ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With the Brewers crowned World Series champions, the 2026-27 offseason is underway. We're  still waiting for the first significant free agent signing or trade, which isn't unusual less than a week into the offseason. Give it another week or so and the action will pick up. Before the hot stove really gets burning, here are 10 bold predictions for the 2026-27 offseason. Remember, all geniuses were called crazy at first.      Skubal's contract is closer to $400M than $300M   
Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Dodgers is the largest pitching contract in history, and our first bold prediction says Tarik Skubal, this offseason's undisputed No. 1 free agent, will beat that. Specifically, he'll sign a contract that is closer to $400 million in value than $300 million, which is another way of saying he'll clear $350 million and break Yamamoto's record for total dollars by a good bit. Scott Boras, Skubal's agent, likes to break contract records with room to spare, not just by a tiny bit. Skubal is the best free agent starter since Yamamoto, and the best free agent starter with MLB experience since Gerrit Cole in 2019. It's a very thin free agent class with few places to (wisely) spend money. The bet here is a team steps up and gives Skubal a record deal.   
        
            
                Tarik Skubal contract predictions: Ace's new deal could break multiple MLB records for a pitcher
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
       Brewers keep and extend Contreras   
Milwaukee's thing over the last few years has been trading its top players a year before free agency (Corbin Burnes, Freddy Peralta, Devin Williams, etc.) and obviously it has worked for them. William Contreras is at that point now: he's scheduled to hit the open market next offseason. This next bold prediction says the Brewers will buck that trend and instead sign the World Series MVP to a long-term extension that keeps him in Milwaukee for at least another few years, if not the rest of his career. How does six years at $24 million a pop sound? That would be $144 million total and the richest contract given to a catcher in the last 13 years, clearing Will Smith's $140 extension with the Dodgers. The World Series champs keep their most irreplaceable player. It has been foretold.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
       Astros keep Paredes, trade Peña   
Every offseason is important, and this one is extra important for new Astros GM Randy Flores, who must figure out what to do with third baseman Isaac Paredes and shortstop Jeremy Peña, both a year away from free agency. Keeping Peña and trading Paredes, and installing Carlos Correa at the hot corner, is the sensible move. This bold prediction says the opposite will happen. The Astros will trade Peña and keep Paredes, and figure out their 2027 infield alignment later. Houston needs help up and down the roster, particularly on the mound, and I think the offers for Peña will simply be too great for Flores to ignore. It will be similar to the Kyle Tucker trade two years ago. The Astros don't have to move Peña, but the offers will get to a point where they just can't say no.   

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Braves trade a member of their core   On one hand, keeping the offense intact and adding some pitching would be a viable offseason plan for the Braves. On the other hand, can they really run it back with the same offense that flatlined after June 1 and in the NLDS? It might be time to shake things up a bit, and I boldly predict it will happen. Ronald Acuña Jr., Drake Baldwin, Michael Harris II, and Matt Olson aren't going anywhere. No team will take the current version of Austin Riley and the six years (!) remaining on his contract. That leaves Ozzie Albies and I suppose Sean Murphy, though the latter is well into role player status now. Does that make this bold prediction a "the Braves will trade Albies" prediction? Yeah, I guess it does. It feels like things are getting a little stale in Atlanta and it's time to change up a core.      Rogers gets a larger contract than Peralta   
You could argue Freddy Peralta is the second-best free agent starter behind Skubal. You could also argue it's Trevor Rogers, who doesn't have Peralta's pedigree or track record, but has strong under-the-hood performance indicators, the kind that project well into the future and get players paid. So, for this bold prediction, I'll say that Rogers signs a richer deal than Peralta, even though the latter is the more famous player and has been better in their careers to date. It'll be close. I can see Rogers getting something in the $125 million range and Peralta signing for right around $120 million, but, in the end, Rogers will sign for more guaranteed dollars because he's a year and a half younger and teams love nothing more than players they believe have untapped upside. That's Rogers, not Peralta.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
       Teoscar returns to Toronto   
After the Dodgers swept in the NLCS, there were calls to infuse some youth into the roster, and, honestly, they need it. Fortunately, Los Angeles has one of the best prospects in the game in the precocious Josue De Paula, who was so impressive late in the season. Trading an outfielder to clear a spot for De Paula seems like such an obvious move that I'm not sure this prediction qualifies as bold. Andy Pages and Kyle Tucker aren't going anywhere, which leaves Teoscar Hernández. How about a trade that sends Hernández back to the Blue Jays? It's a one-year commitment, the Blue Jays badly need over-the-fence power, and the fan base already loves the guy. Teoscar to Toronto as what amounts to their George Springer replacement. I boldly predict it.   

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
       Cubs and Yankees make a trade   Every offseason, there are two teams that appear to match up so well that a trade feels inevitable. Last offseason, it was the Brewers and Mets for a Freddy Peralta deal. This offseason, it's the Cubs and Yankees. The Cubs need rotation help and have some young position players to spare (like Matt Shaw). The Yankees need infield help and have starting pitching to trade (like Will Warren). I'm not saying Shaw for Warren will happen or even should happen. I'm just saying Chicago's and New York's trade chips and roster needs align very well, and when that happens, a trade typically comes together. This bold prediction says the Cubs will send a position player to the Yankees for a starting pitcher, with maybe some other pieces involved on both sides.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
       Mariners swap an arm for a bat   There are trade rumors involving a Mariners starting pitcher every offseason and there's a good reason for that. They have a lot of really good starters and teams want them. The Mariners currently have Kade Anderson, Logan Gilbert, Emerson Hancock, George Kirby, Bryce Miller, and Bryan Woo lined up for their 2027 rotation. They could keep them all because pitching depth has a way of disappearing, sure, but Seattle needed another bat even before Randy Arozarena became a free agent. This next bold prediction says the Mariners finally trade one of their starters in an arm-for-bat deal. I'll say Kirby, who is two years away from free agency, is the one to go. Gilbert is a one-year rental but the better pitcher. The others all have longer control than Kirby.      Sato doubles up Murakami   After coming out of the gate so well in April and May, Munetaka Murakami finished right where the pundits expected. He hit .207 and had the highest strikeout rate among qualified hitters, but he also slugged 35 home runs in only 127 games. Hanshin Tigers third baseman Teruaki Sato, who will be posted for MLB teams this offseason, is similar to Murakami as a strikeout-prone lefty with huge power. This bold prediction says Sato will double Murakami's contract with the White Sox (two years and $34 million) because he's a better bet to stay at third base, a position that is barren in free agency, and because Murakami provided proof of concept. He showed that a player with big contact concerns in Japan can indeed succeed stateside, even if it is an eyesore at times. Four years and $68 million for Sato, perhaps with an opt out that makes the $68 million not really $68 million.   
   Seven of our top 10 free agents will sign before Dec. 1   Dec. 1 is of course when the collective bargaining agreement expires and the owners are expected to lock out the players. My final bold prediction says free agents and teams will get out ahead of the potential lockout and sign in November. Players won't want to wait until who knows when to sign and teams will want to lock in contracts so they can be grandfathered into whatever the next CBA brings. MLB free agency tends to be slow-moving. Last offseason, only one of our top 10 free agents signed in November, and that was Shota Imanaga taking the qualifying offer. Only three other top 10 free agents signed in December. The other six signed on Jan. 14 or later. This offseason will be the opposite, I boldly predict. There will be a flurry of activity in November and at least seven of our top 10 free agents will put pen to paper before a potential lockout.

title: Tyler Huntley out for season: Ravens lose top backup with Lamar Jackson already out, per report - CBS Sports
description: Baltimore will start undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano on Thursday
body:
Baltimore will start undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano on Thursday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:48 am ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        As the reeling Baltimore Ravens try to figure out whether Lamar Jackson's thumb injury will cost him the rest of the season, they got certainty on his backup. Tyler Huntley is in fact out for the remainder of 2026 due to a turf toe injury he suffered after relieving Jackson in Sunday's loss to the Bills, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.The Ravens have been in scramble mode ever since the pair of quarterback injuries. Emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano, an undrafted rookie out of UConn, finished out Sunday's 36-10 blowout loss and will start Thursday against the Jaguars. Baltimore added Austin Reed, who was with the team in the preseason, to its practice squad and signed Kedon Slovis off Green Bay's practice squad earlier this week in an attempt to build some sort of depth on a short week. Reed has never taken a regular-season snap, and Slovis has taken five.Huntley, 29, has spent six of his seven years with the Ravens after going undrafted in 2020. He has been a crucial depth piece, starting 14 games during his time in Baltimore, including three this year as Jackson dealt with an ankle injury. Huntley guided Baltimore to a win over the Falcons but lost to the Browns and Bengals before Jackson's short-lived return. He suffered the turf toe injury when Bills DT Ed Oliver landed on the back of his foot.
With more clarity on at least one quarterback's injury, the Ravens could look to make a trade ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, with Tyson Bagent and Jacoby Brissett as potential options mentioned by NFL Network's Ian Rapoport earlier this week.
Baltimore is 4-4 on the season and has lost three straight games.

title: Midseason All-Rookie Team: QB Jalon Daniels leads team filled with multiple Browns, Jets - CBS Sports
description: The departure from a 16-game regular season eliminated a clean midway point to the NFL regular season, but there is a large enough sampl
body:
The departure from a 16-game regular season eliminated a clean midway point to the NFL regular season, but there is a large enough sample size to assess the contributions of the rookie class through Week 8.Reflecting upon the 2026 NFL Draft, there were 19 offensive and 13 defensive prospects taken in the first round. Although the No. 1 overall selection has yet to make his first start, several others are making a meaningful impact on their respective teams. Here is the Midseason All-Rookie team:Offense
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Quarterback: Jalon Daniels, BuccaneersDaniels is the selection by default. He is the only rookie quarterback to appear in more than one game and the only quarterback with more than 36 dropbacks. The undrafted free agent out of Kansas had some good moments. He looked crisp in three quarters against the Steelers, but accuracy waned in the game's most critical moments. His comfort is throwing to the boundary rather than attacking the middle of the field, but he would lock onto his first read, and defenders began breaking on it once they picked up on the tendency. When the sea parted before him, Daniels showed the foot speed to get chunks of yardage on the ground. 
To be a viable quarterback long-term, Daniels must do a better job handling pressure. He was sacked nine times on 123 dropbacks because the protection was either not set to handle the blitz or he could not feel the pressure on his back. He completed 60 of 98 pass attempts for 501 yards, three touchdowns, and five interceptions. Preseason selection: Fernando Mendoza, Raiders
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Running back: Jeremiyah Love, CardinalsThe running back position was more complicated than quarterback because each of the candidates has either missed time due to injury or is serving in a reserve role. Love leads all rookie running backs with 76 carries despite missing two games and is now actively dealing with an ankle injury that landed him on the injured reserve. His presence on the end-of-year All-Rookie team is very much in doubt. 
Love shows good vision and does well breaking his feet down in space to leverage defenders. He is patient before making his move and has 11 receptions as well. Arizona's offensive line has left a lot to be desired. The Notre Dame product has been averaging 1.1 yards before contact this season, which is below average, according to TruMedia.Las Vegas' Mike Washington Jr. has had some big runs on stretch plays to the boundary. San Francisco's Kaelon Black drew heavy consideration. Denver's Jonah Coleman has been a personal favorite, but the body of work is limited due to injury.Preseason selection: Jeremiyah Love, Cardinals
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Wide receiver: K.C. Concepcion, BrownsConcepcion has the second-most receptions among rookie receivers but has nearly half of his receptions and 57.7% of his receiving yards over the past three games. It has taken some time to develop timing and chemistry with Deshaun Watson, who was errant on several passes in Concepcion's direction at the start of the season. 
Among all rookie receivers, Concepcion ranks second in yards after the catch per reception (5.5), according to TruMedia. He is dynamic and elusive with the ball in his hands. The Texas A&M product has 33 receptions for 352 yards. 
Preseason selection: K.C. Concepcion, Browns
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Wide receiver: Carnell Tate, TitansTate was the third choice, and the margins may be slimmer than one may expect of the leading rookie receiver. The No. 4 overall selection has four drops and three fumbles this season. Tate has good size and the foot quickness to win out of the stem, but he generally has not been threatening downfield against man coverage. He was unavailable for Sunday's loss to the Bengals due to a shoulder injury; the first game of his career missed. 
The Ohio State product leads all rookies in receptions (34) and receiving yards (413). Preseason selection: Carnell Tate, Titans
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Wide receiver: Denzel Boston, BrownsBoston has slowed down a bit over the past month after his blistering start that led to some glamorous statistical and play-style comparisons. Most of his early season success was isolated to ball-winning downfield plays. In each of the first five games, he had a reception of at least 20 yards. In that metric, among rookies, he trails only his teammate, Concepcion, who has seven. Boston is a classic X-receiver, but the Browns would be better served diversifying his usage as he becomes more comfortable transitioning to the NFL. The next step in Boston's growth is developing better chemistry with Watson and finishing plays. Boston has just one drop to his name, but there were a handful of others that could be classified as such. He is consistently open and a zone coverage merchant, but not always on the same page as his quarterback. 
There are a variety of other pass catchers who deserve recognition, such as Omar Cooper Jr. (Jets), Germie Bernard (Steelers), Caleb Douglas (Dolphins), Antonio Williams (Commanders) and Malachi Fields (Giants). Preseason selection: Denzel Boston, Browns
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tight end: Kenyon Sadiq, JetsSadiq has been a plus performer in both the pass and run games. He leads all rookie tight ends in receptions (17) and receiving yards (186). As a prospect, the ex-Oregon Duck was known for his play-making ability post-catch, and he has carried that trait into the league. Among all receivers and tight ends, Sadiq ranks second in yards after the catch per reception (6.0). In the run game, he is a bulldog. He is constantly working and straining to sustain blocks and spring his teammates for bigger gains. At times, he could rein in that energy a bit better, but he has been a well-rounded asset for the AFC franchise. 
In the preseason, Patriots tight end Eli Raridon was among those under consideration. He has been excellent for a rejuvenated New England team. Preseason selection: Kenyon Sadiq, Jets
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Left tackle: Spencer Fano, BrownsThere have been a few rookies to moonlight as left tackles this season, but the possibilities boiled down to Kahlil Benson of the Chiefs, Jayden Williams of the Cardinals and Fano. Benson is a great story and incredibly valuable in the absence of former first-round pick Josh Simmons. However, Fano has a higher ceiling because of his athleticism. Fano has a really natural feel for the game. He communicates and picks up exchanges well. He possesses the requisite foot quickness and ankle flexion to handle most of what is thrown at him. His issues are largely correctable, but his play strength still must improve. 
Fano has been credited with two sacks and 18 pressures allowed on 311 pass-blocking snaps, according to TruMedia. Preseason selection: Spencer Fano, Browns
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Left guard: Kadyn Proctor, DolphinsJacksonville's Emmanuel Pregnon and Proctor were candidates for different reasons. Pregnon has a better feel for the offense and consistently executes it well but does not possess Proctor's ceiling. The former Alabama left tackle has allowed nine pressures and one sack in 186 pass-blocking snaps, according to TruMedia. 
Preseason selection: Kadyn Proctor, Dolphins
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Center: Jake Slaughter, ChargersA training camp injury to veteran Tyler Biadasz forced Slaughter into the starting lineup. Los Angeles' offensive woes can not be attributed to a single person, but the rookie has certainly been a flawed part of the line. TruMedia credits him with eight pressures and one sack allowed on 261 pass-blocking snaps, but more powerful interior players have given him fits with the bull rush. Slaughter has good foot mobility and can execute some of the blocks in space that have been asked of him. Preseason selection: Jake Slaughter, Chargers
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Right guard: Vega Ioane, RavensThere was consideration to pencil in Ioane as the center given he spent some time there this season, which would allow Cleveland's Austin Barber to be the selection at right guard. Ioane and Barber have been the two best interior linemen this season. Baltimore intends to play the former at right guard, so he will align there in this exercise.Although he is now dealing with an injury, TruMedia credits Ioane with seven pressures and one sack allowed on 210 pass-blocking snaps. Ioane plays with a sturdy base and looks for work when disengaged. 
Preseason selection: Francis Mauigoa, Giants
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Right tackle: Blake Miller, LionsMiller struggled in the preseason, which did not inspire much confidence. To his credit, he has responded and performed adequately for the Lions' offensive line. TruMedia credits him with one sack and 13 pressures allowed on 226 pass-blocking snaps. Pittsburgh's run game has been a catalyst for the team's success, and Max Iheanachor's growth at right tackle is a contributing factor. Preseason selection: Monroe Freeling, PanthersDefense
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Defensive tackle: Gracen Halton, 49ersHalton has been impactful in the run and pass games. He has three run stuffs, which is the second-most among rookie interior defenders. He has also turned eight pressures into two sacks. San Francisco drafted two defensive tackles last season, but it has been Halton giving the NFC franchise a jolt. Preseason selection: Kayden McDonald, Texans
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Defensive tackle: Skyler Gill-Howard, LionsGill-Howard is not contributing much in the run game, but his 15 pressures and two sacks lead all rookie interior defenders. He got the final nod over the Jets' Darrell Jackson Jr.. Gill-Howard's value is exceeding his sixth-round selection for a franchise fighting to keep pace in the NFC North.Preseason selection: Christen Miller, Saints
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Edge rusher: David Bailey, Jets Bailey leads all rookies with 5.5 sacks and 26 pressures. The first-year player out of Texas Tech has a spin move that he likes to use, but diversifying that rush plan will be the next stage of growth. He shows an ability to set the edge in the run game and has some violence in his hands but occasionally loses gap discipline. His 15.4% pressure rate is best among rookies, according to TruMedia. Preseason selection: David Bailey, Jets
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Edge rusher: Gabe Jacas, PatriotsJacas has been a ball of energy for the Patriots. He has shown an ability to win with a variety of moves but will also play down the line to finish plays on the backside. Jacas has good speed and power and can break down blocks. He has been a personal favorite at the position thus far. According to TruMedia, Jacas has a 15.0% pressure rate, which is second-best among rookies with at least 100 pass rushing snaps, according to TruMedia. He also ranks second in pressures (23) and sacks (3.0). Preseason selection: Reuben Bain Jr., Buccaneers
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Linebacker: Arvell Reese, GiantsThe options at linebacker are plentiful. Reese plays square to the line of scrimmage and is able to slip blocks to fit run gaps. He has some shock in his hands and does well setting up pass rush moves when his number is called. The injury to quarterback Jaxson Dart could have effectively ended New York's season, but players like Reese have stepped up. He is a well-rounded prospect with elite athleticism. The Giants could honestly utilize him more as a pass rusher, but there is no need given the presence of Kayvon Thibodeaux, Abdul Carter and Brian Burns.Preseason selection: Arvell Reese, Giants
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Linebacker: Sonny Styles, CommandersStyles looks like he stepped out of central casting for an NFL linebacker. He is a fluid athlete who is able to build speed quickly and trail in coverage. Defensive coordinator Daronte Jones hails from the Brian Flores coaching tree, so Styles has been a part of the rush plan. He has just 45 pass rush snaps, but has converted eight of those into pressure. He has 54 tackles, one sack, one forced fumble and one interception ths year. Preseason selection: Sonny Styles, Commanders
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Linebacker: Kendal Daniels, FalconsOne benefit to being the writer of a story is the creative liberties that come with it. In the preseason, a third cornerback spot was incorporated to get Caleb Downs on the field, but the linebacker group has been the most impressive, so this team will incorporate three. Admittedly, I was not the biggest fan of Daniels as a prospect. He looked a bit stiff to fulfill a safety role but also did not look like a natural fit at linebacker. The Oklahoma product does a good job slipping blocks to fit run gaps and rush the passer. He has the range to play sideline to sideline. Daniels has 53 tackles, one sack, one fumble recovery and one interception. Tampa Bay's Josiah Trotter, Miami's Jacob Rodriguez, Tennessee's Anthony Hill Jr. and Daniels' teammate, Harold Perkins Jr., have also represented the position well. Preseason selection: Caleb Downs, Cowboys
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cornerback: Mansoor Delane, ChiefsDelane was one of the easiest selections for the team. He is aggressive playing downhill in run support, but also has elite awareness of his surroundings. The No. 6 overall selection builds speed quickly to stay in-phase and is physical at the line of scrimmage. Delane is at his best playing the ball on arrival. It was a long day at the office against Jaxon Smith-Njigba, but that is true of most any cornerback. Eighty-nine of his 227 receiving yards allowed were against the Seahawks, according to TruMedia. Preseason selection: Mansoor Delane, Chiefs
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cornerback: Malik Muhammad, BearsThere have been multiple cornerbacks who have expressed potential this season: Hezekiah Masses (Raiders), Brandon Cisse (Packers), Davison Igbinosun (Bills), Will Lee III (Panthers) and Muhammad. Muhammad had been present in first-round mock drafts in the past, but faltered in his final season with the Longhorns. Injuries in the Bears secondary led to Muhammad being called into action, but he has made the most of his opportunity. Muhammad must do a better job finishing tackle attempts. He has a 19.2% missed tackle rate, according to TruMedia. Preseason selection: Brandon Cisse, Packers
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Safety: Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, BrownsCleveland has slowly expanded upon McNeil-Warren's role. He has lined up over the slot at times and, at other times, has been the single-high safety. His breakout game was on "Thursday Night Football" against the Steelers, but ironically, Pittsburgh humbled him a bit in Week 8. McNeil-Warren has great range and has shown that in his ability to close on the football. The former MAC star should have recorded his first career interception and returned it for a touchdown against the Ravens, but he was busy planning his celebration before securing the catch. Preseason selection: Dillon Thieneman, Bears
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Safety: Zakee Wheatley, PanthersWheatley has been reliable for the Panthers defense. There are few wasted steps in coverage, and he is rarely out of position. The safety can do a better job wrapping up tackles but plays square to the line of scrimmage. Carolina has been riddled with injuries, particularly in the secondary. The presence of veterans Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn would make life a lot easier for the rookie. Wheatley has one interception and one forced fumble to his name.Pittsburgh's Robert Spears-Jennings has outperformed his seventh-round selection. He should earn more playing time over the second half of the season. Chicago's Dillon Thieneman is also worth acknowledgment. Preseason selection: Treydan Stukes, Raiders
